newsitem.title: USA: American Home offers low-dose contraceptive.
newsitem.headline: American Home offers low-dose contraceptive.

text.p: American Home Products Corp's Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories said Thursday its new low-dose oral contraceptive called Alesse is now available.
The company said Alesse contains a one-third lower dose of the formulation used in the world's most widely prescribed birth control pill combination.

The company said Alesse contains 100 mcg of the progestin levonorgestrel, the most widely prescribed contraceptive progestin, and 20 mcg of ethinyl estradiol, the estrogen most frequently used in oral contraceptives.
The company did not disclose expected revenues from Alesse.
It said more than 40 percent of oral contraceptive prescriptions worldwide contain levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol.
It also said Allese has proven to be 99 percent effective when taken as directed.
